newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo shares run ahead, funds continue buying spree.
newsitem.headline: Oslo shares run ahead, funds continue buying spree.

text.p: Norwegian shares raced to new highs in bumper trade on Tuesday as mutual funds continued to plough into the market before year-end. Dealers said the healthy economic outlook, lower interest rates and a stronger Norwegian crown also contributed to the firm sentiment.
Oslo's Total share index jumped more than one percent to close 9.53 points up at 949.22 points. It had hit a new all-time high at 950.34 points. Turnover was 1.11 billion crowns.
The rally was led by the blue chips with industrial giant Norsk Hydro steaming ahead 5.50 crowns to 333 crowns in business worth 234 million crowns.
Dealers said Hydro's trade was likely spurred on by a strategy presentation to the market.
Shipbuilding and engineering group Kvaerner also powered ahead, the A stock rising four crowns to 276 crowns and the Bs gaining five crowns to 255 crowns.
Trading in oil company Saga Petroleum remained suspended in expectations of an announcement on the takeover of British-based exploration firm Santa Fe Exploration.
Saga said it supervisory board approved the acquisition proposal at a meeting late on Monday.
